chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Dissimulation (Taqiyya) is from the Religion of Allah.' I said, 'From the Religion of Allah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, by Allah! From the Religion of Allah. And indeed, Yusuf (peace be upon him) said, "O caravan! You are indeed thieves." By Allah! They had not stolen anything. And indeed, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said, "I am sick." By Allah! He was not sick.'

key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Dissimulation or concealment of one's true belief or status to avoid harm

ai.seo_question: What is the theological basis for Taqiyya in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates *Taqiyya* from a mere legal precaution to an intrinsic component of divine religion (*min din Allah*), using the prophetic examples of Yusuf and Ibrahim to demonstrate that temporary concealment of truth is a validated spiritual practice. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly view that *Taqiyya* is not merely a political tool for survival but a theological principle rooted in the actions of the Prophets themselves, ensuring the preservation of faith during times of persecution.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Baseer who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The dissimulation (Taqiyya) is from the Religion of Allahazwj’. I said, ‘From the Religion of Allahazwj?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, by Allahazwj! From the Religion of Allahazwj, and Yusufas has said [12:70] O caravan! You are stealing. By Allahazwj! They had not stolen anything. And Ibrahimas had said [37:89] Then he said: I feel sick. By Allahazwj! Heas was not sick’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama’a from abu Basir who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Al-Taqiyyah is of the religion of Allah.’ I asked, ‘Is it of the religion of Allah?’ The Imam said, ‘Yes, by Allah, it is of the religion of Allah. Yusuf (the prophet) had said, ‘O people of the caravan of camels, you are thieves.’ By Allah, they had not stolen anything and Ibrahim had said, ‘I am ill’, by Allah, he had no illness.’”
